pr_title: string-util: fix build error on aarch64
pr_body:
This fixes the following error:
```
In file included from ../src/basic/af-list.h:6,
                 from ../src/basic/af-list.c:7:
../src/basic/string-util.h: In function 'char_is_cc':
../src/basic/string-util.h:133:19: error: comparison is always true due to limited range of data type [-Werror=type-limits]
  133 |         return (p >= 0 && p < ' ') || p == 127;
      |                   ^~
cc1: all warnings being treated as errors
```

Fixes #19543.
pr_comments:
Fun thing, I actually suspected this would break here:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18863#discussion_r622582454

cc @keszybz

review_comments: it might make sense to cast both the lhs *and* the rhs of the `<` comparison. i mean, according to the C standard comparing an unsigned with a signed variable means both are cast to unsigned, so this fix works correctly, but it takes quite some knowledge of C to know that these are the rules.
